text:
Anya: Heads-up — I see a 7% drop in prefix cache hit-rate on prod after yesterday's tokenizer upgrade and system prompt tweak. Traces look like mismatched keys.
Ben: Same. Most misses are for short-chat flows (<= 40 tokens). Hit-rate from 62% -> 55% for chat-legacy route.
Anya: Hypothesis: tokenizer v2 changed whitespace normalization + we started including function_call.name in cache key (recent change). That would fragment prefixes.
Sara: Which PR added function_call fields? I thought we only key on prefix+role+model.
Raj: PR #3421 — we extended key to include 'tools' object to support tool-dependent system prompts.
Anya: I'll paste example keys and two raw prompts that previously deduped but now differ.
Anya: ```old_key = hash("system:\nYou are X\n--\nprefix:user:hello")
new_key = hash("system:\nYou are X\n--\nprefix:user:hello\ntools:[{name:\"search\"}]")``` 
Ben: Oof. That will split everything for users that rarely call tools.
Emily: Deploy-bot: deployment 2026-03-15T05:47Z applied service/eng-runtime v1.86 (PR #3421)
Sara: Can we canonicalize tools presence into an optional 'tool_signature' that is only considered when non-empty? Or normalize order & presence?
Raj: We should also pin tokenizer version in key metadata. Add tokenizer:v2 -> key version bump, but preserve backwards compatibility for warmup.
Anya: Warmup idea: run a background job that pre-warms keys mapping v1->v2 by running canonicalization transform for hot prefixes and inserting new keys pointing to same cached value.
Ben: That sounds heavy but doable for top N prefixes per route.
Sara: Also check system prompt edits: small punctuation changes cause misses. We should add a lightweight prompt-normalizer: normalize whitespace, strip trailing punctuation-only differences for system prompt blocks.
Anya: Agree. Prototype normalizer like: ```normalize(s):= collapse_ws(trim(s)); strip_trailing_periods_in_system_blocks(s)``` 
Emily: Deploy-bot: started job warmup/kv-migration for route chat-legacy (eta ~30m)
Raj: We must be careful with function_call argument serialization — current JSON order is non-deterministic. Use sorted keys or stable serializer.
Ben: +1. Also add tokenizer version tag into cache key but as separate metadata to allow lookup fallback: try exact key then fallback to same-prefix with different tokenizer versions.
Anya: Metric proposal: two phased rollouts: (1) short-circuit: server tries fallback lookup on miss for 5% traffic to assess hit recovery, (2) full warmup + canonicalization + rollout.
Sara: Can someone run a quick sim on recent 24h traffic to estimate warmup operations for top 100k prefixes?
Raj: I'll run simulation on staging traces. ETA 2 hours.
Ben: If we can't prewarm everything, fallback on cold misses should trigger async copy-on-hit to new canonicalized key to avoid regen.
Anya: Also propose adding key_version field to metadata: "kver:2026-03-15-v2" so we can debug regressions later.
Emily: Deploy-bot: warmup job completed for chat-legacy; inserted 12.3k keys. Reports: provisional hit-rate up to 59% in sampler.
Sara: Nice. Continue monitoring. Thanks everyone.
Anya: I'll open followup PR to add canonicalizer + tokenizer pin + fallback lookup logic.
Ben: Ping me on the PR, I'll review.
Emily: Deploy-bot: incident metrics alert cleared: prefix-cache-miss-rate on legacy down to 6% over baseline.
Raj: Follow-up: simulation logs attached to thread (s3://redwood-logs/kv-sim/1875000123) - note ordering assumption fixed.
Anya: Great. Let's retro next week if flakiness persists.
